senses.gloss: pr. n. pl. (prob. a contr. of בית תרעא) Bithter (Βιθθηρά), known as Bettar, a town in Southern Palestine, renowned as the centre of the Bar-Kokhba revolution against Hadrian. [As to its situation, v. Neub. Géogr. p. 130; Graetz Gesch. der Jud. IV, 168).
units: <cite ref="Gittin 57a:22">Gitt. 57ᵃ</cite> <he>כרך ב׳</he> the Fortress of B.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5:13">Y. Taan. IV, 69ᵃ</cite> top.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2:4">Lam. R. to II, 2</cite>; <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 4:18">IV, 18</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:5:21">Y. Ber. I, 3ᵈ</cite>, a. fr. <he>הרוגי ב׳</he> those killed in the Bar-Kokhba revolution (whom Hadrian would not allow to be buried).

<cite ref="Mishnah Challah 4:10">Ḥall. IV, 10</cite> (<cite ref="Mishnah Challah 4:11">11</cite>) (Y. ed. <cite ref="B00760"><he>ביתור</he></cite>; ed. Nap. <he>בייתר</he>, Ven. <he>ביתיר</he>) mentioned as a place not belonging to Palestine proper.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:17">Cant. R. to II, 17</cite> <he>בית תר</he>.
